title: Caching per-user authorization decisions with TTL expiry

source.note: Written by the repository author (v0.2 case set).

input.objective: Cut p95 latency of GET /documents/:id, which is dominated by authorization checks against the permissions service.
constraints: The permissions service API is owned by another team and cannot change this quarter.
p95 budget for GET /documents/:id is 120 ms; currently 340 ms.
input.context: Document service (Node.js 20, 12 pods) calls permissions-service.check(userId, docId, action) on every request: ~180 ms p95, 2,500 rps peak. Users share and unshare documents in the web UI; an HR integration removes accounts and group memberships when people leave. The permissions service publishes a message to the Kafka topic `permission-events` on every write. A Redis 7 cluster is already used for sessions.
input.proposed_solution: Add a read-through cache in the existing Redis cluster, keyed by `authz:{userId}:{docId}:{action}`, storing the boolean decision with a 15-minute TTL. On a miss we call permissions-service and store the result. Entries expire on their own, which keeps the document service decoupled from the permissions team's internals and avoids another consumer to operate. Replaying 24 h of access logs gives an 85% hit rate at 15 minutes (78% at 2 minutes), so p95 should drop to ~40 ms. Rollout behind a feature flag, starting with 10% of traffic, with hit-rate and latency dashboards.
input.environment: Kubernetes, 12 replicas, Redis 7 cluster, Kafka 3.6, Node.js 20.
evidence: APM: 71% of request time is spent in permissions-service.check
Log replay hit rate: 85% at 15 min window, 78% at 2 min window

ground_truth.material_issue: Revocations (unshare, role removal, offboarding) stay effective for up to 15 minutes on every pod, because entries only expire by TTL. For authorization data staleness is a security bug. Fix: event-driven invalidation from the existing permission events (or versioned keys) with TTL only as a backstop, and never cache in a way that can fail open.
required_observations: Revocations (unshare/offboarding) remain effective until TTL expiry
Invalidate from permission-events (or versioned keys); TTL only as backstop
ground_truth.notes: Flaw: TTL-only invalidation on authz data. Direction (caching) is fine, so MODIFY is expected.
